title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's sequel to the Longue Marche, in the part of the notes on 'multiplicities' (stacks) indexed by rho, sigma. Rho and sigma plausibly correspond to the orbifold points of orders 2 and 3, in a modular or Teichmüller setting over a base Sigma_0. The underlined M_{rho,sigma} and its variant M^natural_{rho,sigma} are group objects. The previous page gives the exact sequences 1 -> SN_rho x SZ_sigma x G^+ -> M_{rho,sigma} -> D_12^* -> 1 and 1 -> SN_rho x SZ_sigma -> Gamma_{rho,sigma} -> D_12^* -> 1. It also gives SN_rho = mu_rho, isomorphic to {+-1}_{Sigma_0}, and SZ_sigma isomorphic to G_0 (on the next page G_0 seems to be G_m). Finally it lists semi-direct decompositions such as Z_{rho,sigma} = D_12^* . G_0 and N_rho/mu_rho = D_12^*.

On this page Grothendieck divides out the central mu_rho and uses those splittings. He obtains canonical isomorphisms (195):
- M_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho is isomorphic to D_12^* . (G_0 x G^+);
- M^natural_{rho,sigma}/mu_rho is isomorphic to D_12^* . (G_0 x M), where G^natural = M;
- Gamma_{rho,sigma} is isomorphic to D_12^* . G_0.
Here the dot denotes a semi-direct product, the same notation as in (194) on the previous page. It is not a quotient. D_12^* acts on G_0 and on G^+ through the actions written earlier as (181) and (151); the margin note says the same.

The groups M and M^natural themselves are mu_rho-coverings of these semi-direct products. Grothendieck says they are recovered from the extension (196), 1 -> mu_rho -> N_rho -> D_12^* -> 1, by pulling back along the projections of the groups (195) onto their D_12^* factor. Equivalently, M_{rho,sigma} is (N_rho x_{D_12^*} (D_12^* . (G_0 x G^+))), with the semi-direct structure lifted.

He then conjectures ('sûrement') that (196) is itself pulled back from an extension of (mu x mu)_{Sigma_0} by mu. The pullback map would be the pair of sign characters (epsilon_2, epsilon_3): D_12^* -> (mu x mu)_{Sigma_0}, compared with §49 V 8°. Read D_12 as the dihedral group of order 12, the automorphisms of the hexagonal lattice. Then D_12 is S_3 x Z/2 and its abelianization is (Z/2)^2. The restriction H^*((Z/2)^2, F_2) -> H^*(S_3 x Z/2, F_2) along the abelianization map is an isomorphism, since the order-3 subgroup is invisible mod 2. So every central extension by Z/2 is indeed pulled back from (Z/2)^2, at least in the constant case, and the conjecture holds. The page as a whole is a structural bookkeeping step. It prepares the definition of the sub-multiplicities M_{rho,sigma}[0], (0), (1/2) on the next page.
errors: The target group symbol is written inconsistently across the pages: O_12, O_12^*, O_12^x, D_12^*. It is the same group, notation drifting.
Equation numbers (195) and (196) are reused for different formulas on the next page (numbering clash).

No real mathematical gap. The 'sûrement' claim about (196) is justified if D_12^* is the dihedral group of order 12 (S_3 x Z/2), via the mod-2 cohomology isomorphism. Over a non-constant base Sigma_0 one would also need the twisted-form version.

ideas.what: Presenting a group-multiplicity, modulo a central mu_2, as a semi-direct product of a finite dihedral-type group with G_0 x G^+.
ideas.modern_name: Semi-direct product decomposition of a group stack / normalizer structure

ideas.what: Recovering a central mu_2-extension by pulling back a fixed extension of the finite quotient.
Conjecture that the extension of D_12^* by mu factors through its abelianization via the two sign characters (epsilon_2, epsilon_3).
ideas.modern_name: Mod-2 cohomology of D_12 = S_3 x Z/2 detected on abelianization

deep.surprise_reason: Routine structural bookkeeping of extensions and semi-direct products inside a long technical computation. The only open remark (factoring (196) through (mu x mu)) follows from standard mod-2 group cohomology.
transcription_corrections: In (195) the symbol is a semi-direct product dot, 'D_12^* · (G_0 x G^+)', not a quotient 'D_12^* \ (G_0 x G^+)'. The same holds for the other two lines.
First line of (195): something after M_{rho,sigma} is struck through before '/mu_rho'.
The group symbol is a double-struck D/O with subscript 12, consistent with 'O_12^*' on the previous page. In the margin it is D_12^* (or O_12^*).
Under (195) an underbrace identifies G_0 x M with G_0 x G^natural, written as G_0 x G^+ type; it is not a parenthetical comment.
The margin note reads approximately: 'op. de D_12^* sur G_0 x G^+ donnée via (181) et (151). Sur G_0 x M [struck], D_12^* opère via ... et ... simplement par ...'. The ending is partly illegible.
In the final lines, 'que j'ai explicitées [-dans-] plus haut (181) et (151)' is correct, with '(18?)' read as (181).
